newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Great Ocean to issue new B shares.
newsitem.headline: China Great Ocean to issue new B shares.

text.p: Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said on Monday it has been given the green light by shareholders to offer 50 million additional B shares.

Three shareholders representing 108.041 million shares, or 60.02 percent of the company's total share capital of 180 million shares, approved the proposal at a meeting last week, said a company statement in Monday's Securities Times.
The pricing and timing of the issue have yet to be decided, the firm said without giving further details.
The company said last month it planned to issue 50 million new B shares in 1997 and list them on the Shenzhen exchange.

The offer, tentatively priced at between HK$2.50-3.50 per share, requires final approval by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, it said, adding it would use funds from the offer to buy container ships.

A company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the firm estimated 1996 after-tax profits would be less than 43 million yuan, compared with 50.39 million yuan in 1995 and 39.75 million yuan in 1994.
He said the company's net profit fell in 1996 due to China's sluggish exports.
The official expected strong growth in the company's net earnings in 1997 after an expected export recovery and the firm's own efforts to expand its key shipping agency business.
